question: T009d caught the Angular 13 lane of pigallery2 dying on "ReferenceError: $localize is not defined" before bootstrap, and said in its own notEstablished that it had NOT established that adding @angular/localize/init is sufficient, because that build was never attempted.

This unit performs exactly that standard Angular 9+ migration step - nothing more - rebuilds the lane twice, and re-witnesses both lanes live against the same era backend in the same session. The question is narrow and falsifiable: does the standard step close the defect, and does the lane then run?
answerInOneLine: The standard step closes the $localize defect COMPLETELY and exposes a second one behind it: the lane now bootstraps and routes itself, then dies on "Error: Cannot find module './messages.en-US.xlf'" from a DI factory, never reaches its gallery, and makes ZERO API calls - while the outcome strings, for the first time, read identical: true. Read that parity flag as the warning it is.

headline.howThatIsKnown: the migrated lane no longer sits on "/". Its running application navigated itself to "/login" - Angular's router ran, which it cannot do unless the module bootstrapped. In T009d the application never moved off "/" because it never started.
headline.whatItStillCannotDo: reach its gallery. galleryComponentPresent false, gridPresent false, photoTiles 0, navbarPresent false, visibleText empty, and ZERO calls to /api/notifications or /api/gallery/content/ - against a baseline lane that does all five.
headline.theTrap: parity.identical is TRUE and the lane is BROKEN. Both lanes now report routes-reached 0 for OPPOSITE reasons: the baseline leaves "/" for /gallery/ (healthy), the migrated leaves "/" for /login (broken). The outcome vocabulary cannot tell those apart. Anything downstream that prices a pigallery2 claim on parity.identical alone would price this lane as GREEN.

The schematic touched exactly the two files above and the lock file. So the claim "the STANDARD step, and only the standard step" is literal here, not a paraphrase.
item8.exactPolyfillsDiff:
+/***************************************************************************************************
+ * Load `$localize` onto the global scope - used if i18n tags appear in Angular templates.
+ */
+import '@angular/localize/init';
why: Angular 9 moved template i18n from a compile-time ViewEngine transform to a RUNTIME tagged-template function named $localize. From v9 on, the AOT compiler emits `$localize\`...\`` tagged constants into the component `consts` of any component carrying i18n attributes - and pigallery2 1.7.0 carries them throughout its templates.

The emitted bundle therefore REFERENCES $localize whether or not the application ever translates anything. Nothing in @angular/core defines it; the tag lives in the separate @angular/localize package and is installed onto the global scope only by importing @angular/localize/init before bootstrap. That is why the CLI puts the import in polyfills.ts and why `ng add @angular/localize` exists as a first-class migration step.

This is measurable in the artefacts, not inferred: the migrated main bundle contains 215 occurrences of $localize both BEFORE and AFTER the fix (it is byte-identical - see rebuild.mainBundleUnchanged), and the polyfills bundle contains 0 before and 2 after, one of which is the assignment that defines the tag globally.
item8.whereTheFirstEmittedTagSits: main.4b2fa472bc230245.js offset 241780, inside the `consts` factory of the app-login component: `t=$localize`:\u241f380bac8029fe968edf74d1856635666bf8b55516\u241f1692815930495952260:Please log in`` - within eight bytes of the 241772 column T009d's ReferenceError named. The catch and the fix point at the same place in the same bundle.

parity.comparedOn: the ordered list of outcome strings each lane produced, string for string, plus the per-journey measured counts behind them. Same comparison T009d made.
parity.changedFromT009d: T009d reported identical false, on two outcome strings. This unit reports identical TRUE. Nothing about the migrated lane's health justifies that flip.
readThisTheRightWayRound: IDENTICAL: TRUE IS NOT GOOD NEWS HERE. The flag flipped because the migrated lane started FAILING DIFFERENTLY, not because it started working.
In T009d the migrated lane never navigated, so it "reached" the declared route "/" and scored routes-reached 1 against the baseline's 0. That mismatch is what made identical false.

In T009e the migrated lane bootstraps and its router navigates itself to /login. It therefore leaves "/" - exactly as the baseline leaves "/" for /gallery/ - and scores routes-reached 0 too. Two lanes, one healthy and one broken, produce the same six strings.

The outcome vocabulary is counting route departures. It cannot see WHERE either lane went, and it cannot see that one arrived at a gallery with three photo tiles while the other arrived at a login screen that rendered nothing at all.
The finding therefore lives in runningApplication and requestsObserved, not in parity - and this record exists partly to say so in a place a downstream consumer cannot miss.

finding.one: THE STANDARD STEP CLOSED THE DEFECT IT NAMES. @angular/localize@13.4.0 + one import line in polyfills.ts removed "ReferenceError: $localize is not defined" entirely, without touching a byte of the application: the main bundle sha256 is unchanged. T009d's open question - is @angular/localize/init sufficient to fix the $localize defect - is answered YES.
finding.two: IT DID NOT MAKE THE LANE WORK. Sufficient for the defect is not sufficient for the migration. Behind the first i18n defect sat a second one, and the lane still cannot show a gallery.

secondDefect.verbatimNote: that is the console message exactly as the witness host recorded it, including the driver's 300-character truncation mid-word at "(ht". Nothing was cleaned up.

whereItComesFrom.wiredAs: {provide: TRANSLATIONS, useFactory: translationsFactory, deps: [LOCALE_ID]} - so the factory runs the first time anything injects TRANSLATIONS, which @ngx-translate/i18n-polyfill's I18n service does.

mechanism: The guard is an exact string test against 'en'. On the baseline lane LOCALE_ID really is 'en', because the era build was invoked with the ViewEngine flag --i18n-locale en; the factory short-circuits and returns an empty string, and nothing is ever required.

Angular 13 has no --i18n-locale flag - T009b already recorded the four --i18n-* flags as dropped with no v13 equivalent, as migration-delta material. With no flag, LOCALE_ID falls back to Angular's built-in default, 'en-US'. 'en-US' !== 'en', the guard misses, and the factory reaches the require.

frontend/translate/ contains messages.en.xlf, messages.fr.xlf, messages.hu.xlf and messages.ru.xlf. There is no messages.en-US.xlf, so webpack's generated require-context throws 'Cannot find module' at runtime, inside DI, and the component being constructed never renders.
secondDefect.whyThisIsTheSameFamily: Both defects are the Angular 9+ i18n rearchitecture arriving late. The first is the runtime tag the new compiler emits and no longer defines for you; the second is a locale the old CLI used to set for you and the new one does not. T009b saw the i18n flags disappear at build time and recorded it; this unit is where that build-time delta becomes a runtime failure.
secondDefect.notFixedHere: deliberately. The packet permits exactly two edits - the dependency and the polyfill import - and forbids anything broader, because the claim under test is that the STANDARD step closes the defect. Setting LOCALE_ID, adding a messages.en-US.xlf, or relaxing the guard are all application changes and a different claim for a different unit.
secondDefect.probableShapeOfTheRealFix: stated as a hypothesis, NOT as a measurement: provide LOCALE_ID as 'en', or widen the factory guard to startsWith('en'). Neither was attempted and neither is established by anything in this record.

finding.three: THE PARITY FLAG WENT GREEN WHILE THE LANE STAYED BROKEN. This is the most transferable thing in the record. A closed outcome vocabulary that counts route departures scored a login-screen-that-renders-nothing identically to a working gallery. Downstream pricing must read runningApplication and apiCallsMade, not parity.identical.
finding.four: DETERMINISM SURVIVED THE FIX. Two independent rebuilds, 13/13 files byte-identical, same webpack hash. Whatever else is wrong with this lane, it is not flaky.

machineTimes.migratedWitnessNote: the migrated lane's ~31s is again almost entirely the two bounded 15s waits timing out - but this time with a RUNNING application on the other side of them.

reproduce: # 1. the fix - the canonical CLI path, one consented fetch
# 3. re-witness both lanes, serialized, baseline first (it derives the plan)
notEstablished: THE MIGRATED LANE IS NOT FIXED. This record establishes that ONE named defect is closed. It establishes the opposite of a working lane: no gallery, no navbar, no grid, zero photo tiles, zero API calls, empty visible text. Nobody may read "identical: true" here as a migration that works.

THE SECOND DEFECT IS DIAGNOSED FROM THE ERROR AND THE SOURCE, NOT FROM A FIX. The mechanism above (LOCALE_ID en-US vs the factory's 'en' guard) is read off the verbatim error string, the application source at app.module.ts:114-123, the contents of frontend/translate/, and T009b's already-recorded loss of the --i18n-* flags. No build was made with a corrected locale, so it is NOT established that setting LOCALE_ID to 'en' makes the lane work, or that a THIRD defect does not sit behind the second. T009d made exactly this mistake's opposite number and named it; the same caution applies here.

WHY THE LANE LANDS ON /login RATHER THAN /gallery/ IS NOT ESTABLISHED. It is recorded as measured. Whether the login redirect is itself a consequence of the translations failure, a separate auth-bootstrap difference, or ordinary routing before the failure, was not investigated.

A THREE-IMAGE GENERATED GALLERY IS NOT THE FLEET'S MEDIA DIVERSITY. Three 64x48 solid-colour PNGs, no EXIF, no GPS, no faces, no video, no nested directories. Nothing here speaks about EXIF parsing, orientation, date grouping, maps, person detection or transcoding.

AUTH SURFACES ARE UNTESTED even though the migrated lane landed on /login. authenticationRequired was false and unAuthenticatedUserRole was Admin; no login was performed and no credential was entered on either lane.

THE DATABASE WAS THE MEMORY BACKEND, NOT SQLITE - identical on both lanes, so it cannot produce the lane difference, but search, sharing and face surfaces were disabled by the application itself on both.
ONE JOURNEY, ONE PASS PER LANE, ONE HOST. Nothing here establishes witness determinism across repeated runs (the BUILD determinism claim is separate and is established, twice over).

THE BASELINE LANE IS STILL NOT CERTIFIED WORKING. It mounts, routes to /gallery/, calls its API twice and renders three photo TILES - photoImages is 0, so no thumbnail is established as generated or displayed. Nothing was clicked.
NO SCREENSHOT, NO PIXEL COMPARISON, NO ACCESSIBILITY READING, NO PERFORMANCE READING.
THE BACKEND IS THE ERA BACKEND ON BOTH LANES. Nothing here says anything about an Angular 13 frontend against a migrated backend; no backend migration exists.
THE CONSOLE MESSAGES ARE TRUNCATED AT 300 CHARACTERS by the reused driver. The full stack below "at Object.c7 [as useFactory] (ht" was never captured, on either lane, in either unit.
NOTHING HERE RE-ESTABLISHES T009a, T009b or T009c. The baseline lane output was consumed as-is and not rebuilt.

supersedes.what: NOTHING. This record does not supersede evidence/runs/angular-13cell/pigallery2-live-witness.json - it EXTENDS it. T009d's catch stands exactly as published: at the build it witnessed, $localize was undefined and the lane never bootstrapped. This unit changed the build, so it reports on a different artefact.
supersedes.closesOpenQuestionFrom: evidence/runs/angular-13cell/pigallery2-live-witness.json notEstablished item "THE MIGRATED LANE'S DEFECT IS NAMED, NOT DIAGNOSED TO ITS ROOT ... It does not establish that adding @angular/localize/init is sufficient to make the lane work, because that build was not attempted here." Answered: sufficient to close the $localize defect, NOT sufficient to make the lane work.

nextUnit: T010 freeze supersession inherits a live-backend parity claim that is numerically GREEN and substantively NEGATIVE. Two things must travel with it: (a) the pigallery2 Angular 13 lane builds deterministically, bootstraps after the standard localize step, and still cannot render its gallery, blocked on a second i18n defect that is named here; (b) parity.identical proved capable of reading true across a working and a broken lane, so any gate that consumes it alone is not measuring what it thinks it is measuring.
